subject: System Design
title: Event-Driven Architecture
description: A fast breakdown of Event-Driven Architecture for builders.

hook.text: A user places an order. Instead of calling 5 services in sequence, one event triggers them all in parallel.

buildup.text: Event-driven systems publish events to a bus. Interested services subscribe and react independently.

discovery.text: This decouples services. The order service doesn't need to know about shipping, billing, or notifications.

twist.text: Debugging is harder. When something fails, tracing across async events requires distributed tracing tools.

climax.text: Event-driven architecture enables loose coupling and high scalability at the cost of observability.

punchline.text: Events decouple services — at the cost of visibility.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of event-driven architecture?
options: Services are decoupled and react independently
